data.title: Cutaneous candidiasis / intertrigo — viva
data.summary: Fungal infections · 11 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Cutaneous candidiasis / intertrigo** (Fungal infections)_

**Q1. What is candidiasis? Main species?**
- Infection by Candida (yeast; commensal of gut, mouth, vagina) when local or systemic defences fail — C. albicans (commonest); non-albicans: C. glabrata, C. tropicalis, C. parapsilosis, C. krusei (fluconazole resistant), Candida auris (multidrug-resistant, hospital outbreaks)
- Dimorphic: yeast, pseudohyphae and true hyphae (in tissue)

**Q2. Predisposing factors.**
- Local: moisture, occlusion, obesity, maceration, friction, dentures, wet work, diapers
- Systemic: diabetes, pregnancy, infancy/old age, antibiotics, steroids, OCP, HIV, immunosuppression, iron deficiency, endocrinopathies (hypoparathyroidism, hypothyroidism, Addison's)

**Q3. Clinical forms of mucocutaneous candidiasis.**
- Oral: pseudomembranous (thrush, removable white plaques), erythematous (atrophic — antibiotic/denture), hyperplastic (leukoplakia-like), angular cheilitis, median rhomboid glossitis
- Genital: vulvovaginitis (curdy discharge, itching), balanoposthitis (diabetics, uncircumcised)
- Skin: intertrigo (flexures), napkin candidiasis, interdigital (erosio interdigitalis blastomycetica — 3rd web space of hand in wet workers), chronic paronychia, onychomycosis
- Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis (CMC); congenital and neonatal candidiasis; disseminated candidiasis (nodules in neutropenic patients)

**Q4. Describe candidal intertrigo.**
- Bright beefy-red moist glazed patches in folds (groin, submammary, axillae, abdominal folds) with fissure at the base, peripheral scaling (collarette) and satellite papulopustules
- Burning/itching; scrotum often involved (unlike tinea cruris)

**Q5. Differential diagnosis of intertrigo.**
- Tinea cruris (active edge, scrotum spared), erythrasma (brown, coral-red fluorescence), inverse psoriasis (well-defined, no satellites), seborrhoeic dermatitis, irritant/allergic contact dermatitis, Hailey–Hailey disease, Langerhans cell histiocytosis (infants), extramammary Paget's (elderly, persistent)

**Q6. What is chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis (CMC)?**
- Group of disorders with persistent/recurrent Candida infections of skin, nails and mucosa due to defective Th17 immunity
- Causes: STAT1 gain-of-function, IL-17RA/IL-17F, CARD9 deficiency, AIRE mutation (APECED/APS-1 — with hypoparathyroidism, Addison's), hyper-IgE (STAT3); thymoma
- Treatment: long-term azoles, treat endocrinopathy

**Q7. Investigations.**
- KOH/Gram stain: budding yeasts with pseudohyphae (pseudohyphae suggest invasion)
- Culture on SDA (creamy colonies); germ tube test (C. albicans positive), CHROMagar for species, antifungal susceptibility for recurrent/non-albicans
- Blood sugar, HIV; in CMC — immunology and endocrine work-up

**Q8. Treatment of cutaneous candidiasis.**
- Keep area dry, separate folds with cotton cloth, weight loss, control diabetes, treat source (oral/gut)
- Topical azoles (clotrimazole, miconazole, ketoconazole), nystatin, ciclopirox; short mild steroid combination only if very inflamed
- Oral fluconazole 150 mg weekly/50–100 mg daily for 1–2 weeks for extensive or recurrent; itraconazole alternative

**Q9. Treatment of vulvovaginal candidiasis.**
- Clotrimazole 500 mg vaginal pessary single dose or 100 mg for 6 nights, or fluconazole 150 mg oral single dose (avoid oral in pregnancy — use topical 7 days)
- Recurrent (≥4/year): fluconazole 150 mg every 72 h × 3 doses, then weekly for 6 months; C. glabrata — boric acid vaginal capsules

**Q10. What is chronic paronychia and its management?**
- Inflammation of proximal nail fold >6 weeks in wet workers; loss of cuticle, bolstered red fold, nail dystrophy; now considered mainly an irritant/eczematous process with Candida as secondary
- Keep hands dry, gloves, topical steroid + azole, treat Candida, avoid cuticle trimming

**Q11. What is Candida auris and why important?**
- Emerging multidrug-resistant yeast, hospital outbreaks, colonises skin, often misidentified by routine methods; needs echinocandin and strict infection control

## Quick spotter facts
- Beefy-red fold with satellite pustules and scrotal involvement — candidal intertrigo
- Erosio interdigitalis blastomycetica — 3rd finger web
- Pseudohyphae on KOH

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Candidiasis). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
